title: O Destitute of All Defence
description: O Destitute of All Defence in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Hymns”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O des-ti-tute of all de-fence, We bow be-fore Thee now; In mer-cy let Thy mer-cy come, For mer-ci-ful art Thou.

lines: O destitute of all defence,
We bow before Thee now;
In mercy let Thy mercy come,
For merciful art Thou.
Our trusting souls in quiet repose
Would rest Thy love within; —
O be not angry with us, Lord,
Nor think upon our sin.
But from Thy high abode look down,
With tender love the while,
And save us from our foes who would
Our wayward hearts beguile.
For, verily Thou art our God,
And we Thy people all; —
Hear us, the creatures of Thy hand,
When on Thy name we call.
To God the Father, God the Son,
All praise and glory be;
And to the Spirit, Three in One,
To all eternity.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
